full_judgment:
5. Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the petitioner, placed before us the impugned judgment of the High Court Division as well as the judgments of the Courts below. In support of the leave-petition, Mr. Nawab Ali contends that the High Court Division failed to consider that the Appellate Court failed to apply its judicial mind in not considering that the plaintiffs are not in possession in the suit property and as such injunction can not be granted to one, who is not in possession thereby the High Court Division having affirmed the decision of the Appellate Court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. 

 6. The next submission made by Mr. Nawab Ali is that the basis of claim of the plaintiff-respondents is Exhibit-4, which is a certified copy of the deed and the original of which having not been filed nor an explanation was given as to where the original document is lying and in such view of the matter, the High Court Division ought to have found that the aforesaid certified copy of the deed Exhibit-4 is not genuine one and the High Court Division having failed to consider this aspect committed and error of law in discharging the Rule and as such the findings and decisions arrived at by the High Court Division are liable to be set aside. 

 8. Mr. Nawab Ali, being confronted with above submissions of the learned Advocate for the respondents, finds difficulty to support the judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissing the plaintiff's suit.
